A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoVAND, NEGTOME and LoRA research. Text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection experiments, component ablations, dataset-scaling analyses and NegBench evaluations, with further experimental results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds biomedical evaluation, token-boosting comparisons and an original dataset audit.

M1.justification: The operational CoVAND pipeline, NEGTOME merging and targeted LoRA recipe are retained. Section 3.2 replaces 'softmax-weighted average' with fixed normalized weighting, matching the already-present Equation 2. Appendix D elaborates implementation and introduces comparison variants, without establishing a changed proposed method.

E1.justification: v2 adds FG-CXR chest X-rays and region-level discrimination between diagnostic captions and polarity-flipped contradictions (Section 4.5; Appendix I). This substantially extends the represented domain and task beyond the retained natural-image detection and NegBench evaluations. No medical training is reported.

E2.justification: New Table S8 evaluates Noun-only Boost, Neg-only Boost, Merge Head Boost and Attn Bias against NEGTOME. These are focused additions to the comparator set; the external detector, MLLM and post-hoc VQA comparisons already present in v1 are retained.

E3.justification: v2 introduces region-wise FG-CXR testing with rule-generated contradictions and max-logit binary accuracy, matched one-epoch CoVAND-L training for the new controls, and a random 1,000-sample Gemini/manual annotation audit. These substantially extend evaluation design; they do not establish revisions to the retained benchmark protocols.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's data, LoRA-placement and merging/boost ablations, v2 directly tests simpler boosting and attention-bias alternatives. Appendices A.3–A.4 add negation-distribution analysis, an annotation-error audit and error examples. FG-CXR additionally tests transfer under substantial visual and linguistic domain shift.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 adds sample-based annotation-error estimation: manual adjudication of 78 disagreements in a 1,000-sample audit identifies 23 dataset errors, yielding a reported 2.3% estimate. Model-performance reporting still adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing main Tables 1–4 and corresponding appendix results remain unchanged. New results include FG-CXR accuracy of 54.86% for G-DINO-B versus 62.55% with the method, Table S8's NEGTOME AP/FPR of 57.3/47.7, and dataset distribution and audit findings. These are additional results under newly reported evaluations, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: The original LoRA equations and cue-amplification argument, including Equation 3, remain unchanged. Appendix D restates weighted pooling and specifies empirical controls; it adds no substantive theoretical argument, assumption, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: instance-grounded negation data, boosted token merging with efficient LoRA adaptation, and improved negation handling and generalization. Biomedical results add support without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning prompt-induced cue imbalance, residual annotation ambiguity, the insufficiency of isolated token boosting and biomedical transfer beyond memorization. Appendix C substantially expands mechanism explanations, including learned-gating and full-rank-expressivity descriptions that are not reconciled with the fixed-weight, low-rank formulation. Earlier complex-negation limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds spaCy-to-subword alignment details, token-selection functions and weighting rules. Appendices A.4 and I document audit logging/adjudication and medical-caption processing. Existing hardware, main training settings and the promise to release code and data upon publication are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix C extensively positions the work against research on CoT data construction, visual grounding, parameter-efficient adaptation, compositional reasoning and bias mitigation. It adds discussions of works such as VideoEspresso, DoRA, RandLoRA and BEND-VLM, substantially expanding the earlier compact related-work treatment.

P1.justification: Most main-text paragraphs are retained, but the appendix gains extensive five-part literature exposition and synthesis, alongside expanded analytical explanations and navigation. Smaller edits clarify pooling terminology, update affiliations and add acknowledgments. This is substantial expository expansion rather than merely renumbering existing sections.

P2.justification: v2 adds a negation-distribution chart, two audit-example figures, the boosting-comparison table and biomedical tables; Table S12 redisplays Table 5's results. Existing figures and tables are largely preserved, with relocation, renumbering and some resizing of wrapped tables rather than a wholesale visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The new boosting controls and biomedical evaluation provide useful evidence about mechanism and transfer that v1 lacked, while the audit exposes concrete annotation errors. These gains are tempered by disagreement-only manual review underlying the claimed 97.7% dataset accuracy, an unexplained 48,761-versus-91,110 caption count, and conflicting learned-gating descriptions in Appendix C. The result is a modest net improvement in evidential coverage, with unresolved reporting weaknesses.
